defaultCreds.title: Check default credentials
defaultCreds.warn: A sharp special feature: CERNIS actively tries to log in to a device using its factory-default credentials. That is a real login attempt — use it only for devices on your own network that belong to you. For safety it is locked by default and must be unlocked here for each session.

defaultCreds.saveError: The unlock state could not be changed.
defaultCreds.dialogBody: Before you unlock this special feature, please read what it does. It deliberately differs from the passive observation features of CERNIS.
defaultCreds.dialogActiveText: CERNIS really logs in using default credentials. This can produce device logs or briefly lock accounts. Use it only on your own devices.
defaultCreds.dialogOwnNetText: Targets outside the private network are rejected by the system.
defaultCreds.dialogSessionText: The unlock applies solely to the current CERNIS session. After a restart the feature is locked again.

lookupDialog.title: Port {{num}}/{{proto}}
lookupDialog.generic: There is no internal description for this port. You can look it up externally via the link below if needed.

info.ftp: FTP transfers files between computers. The classic variant is unencrypted; for sensitive data, FTPS or SFTP is common today.
info.ssh: SSH provides encrypted remote access to a system (console, file transfer, tunnels). A common, encrypted way to manage a host.
info.telnet: Telnet is an early remote-access service and works unencrypted. Nowadays it is mostly replaced by SSH.
info.smtp: SMTP sends email between mail servers. The transport can be secured via STARTTLS.
info.dns: DNS resolves names (e.g. example.com) into IP addresses. A fundamental service of network infrastructure.
info.http: HTTP serves web pages and web APIs. The connection is unencrypted; the secured variant is HTTPS.
info.pop3: POP3 retrieves email from a server. The classic variant is unencrypted; secured it runs over POP3S.
info.netbios: NetBIOS handles name and session management in older Windows networks and is usually confined to the local network.
info.imap: IMAP manages email directly on the server (multiple devices, in sync). Secured it runs over IMAPS.
info.https: HTTPS serves web pages and APIs encrypted (HTTP over TLS). The common, secured way to access the web today.
info.smb: SMB provides file and printer sharing (mainly in Windows networks). Usually only within the local network.
info.ipp: IPP controls printing over the network and carries print jobs and status information.
info.imaps: IMAPS is IMAP over an encrypted TLS connection — secured access to email on the server.
info.pop3s: POP3S is POP3 over an encrypted TLS connection — secured retrieval of email.
info.mqtt: MQTT is a lightweight messaging protocol, common in the context of IoT and sensor devices.
info.mysql: MySQL is a database service. Its access should usually not be openly reachable on the network.
info.rdp: RDP allows graphical remote control of a Windows machine. An RDP endpoint reachable from the internet is considered especially exposed.
info.postgresql: PostgreSQL is a database service. Its access should usually not be openly reachable on the network.
info.vnc: VNC allows graphical remote control of a machine. Depending on the configuration, the connection may be unencrypted.
info.http-alt: An alternative HTTP port, often used for web applications, proxies or management interfaces.

traffic.title: Per-app traffic
traffic.sniHint: Shows the real domain names apps request (instead of just the host). Requires elevated privileges.
traffic.groupLocalHint: Services waiting for connections, and connectionless UDP traffic such as local device discovery. Normal local network behaviour without a peer.
traffic.durchsatzNichtMessbar: On macOS it is not possible to measure how much data an individual program transfers — the operating system provides no interface for this. It cannot be unlocked. What is shown in full, however, is which program talks to which peer.
traffic.durchsatzOhneWerte: No throughput values are currently available for the connections shown. What is displayed are the connections of your own user account.
traffic.durchsatzWerkzeugFehlt: Per-program throughput comes from the system tool ss (package iproute2). It is not present on this system, so the throughput values stay empty. Which program talks to which peer is shown in full.
traffic.durchsatzMessungFehlgeschlagen: The last throughput measurement failed, so no values are available right now. The connection list itself remains fully usable.
traffic.durchsatzRechteVerzicht: Which program talks to which peer is shown in full. How much data an individual program transfers in the process is not shown by CERNIS on Windows: the operating system releases these figures only to programs that run permanently with elevated privileges. CERNIS deliberately does without that.

access.title: Set up capture access
access.intro: To read the actual domain names, CERNIS needs one-time read access to your Mac's capture devices. Your Mac will now ask for your password or Touch ID.
access.onceText: you are asked once, not on every start.
access.limitedText: read access for capturing only. CERNIS still does not run as an administrator.

sni.consentIntro: Often only the host appears, not the actual service behind it. The requested domain name is what makes trackers and ad networks visible. CERNIS can read these names passively:

sni.consentEphemeralText: only while this view is open, nothing is stored.
sni.consentPrivilegeText: set up once, no recurring dialog.

dnsTrust.intro: This function shows the DNS servers CERNIS has observed on your network. Define which servers you expect and in what order, bring detected servers into your expectation, or reject a server. For each server you see a few clues to help you decide.
dnsTrust.redLine: CERNIS shows and classifies, but does not judge. Whether a DNS server is trustworthy is your call — the clues only help.
dnsTrust.empty: No DNS servers detected yet — they appear after the next start or a recording.
dnsTrust.ladeFehler: The DNS servers could not be loaded. Please check whether the backend is running.
dnsTrust.aktionFehler: The decision could not be saved.
dnsTrust.aktionFehlerUnbekannt: This address is not known yet and therefore cannot be rated.
dnsTrust.aktionFehlerNichtBestaetigt: An order can only be assigned to confirmed servers.

expected.title: Expected — ordered
expected.lead: The DNS servers you expect — in your order. The order is your expectation, not a measurement.
expected.empty: No expected DNS server yet. Use “Mark as expected” below to add a detected server.

detected.title: Detected, not yet expected
detected.lead: Servers this machine actually uses or has seen. Decide whether they belong to your expectation.

manual.title: Added manually
manual.lead: DNS servers you entered yourself. They count as expected but have not been observed here yet. As soon as such a server actually shows up, it moves up to the expected servers.

rejected.title: Rejected
rejected.lead: Servers you have rejected. You can revoke the decision at any time.

placeholder.note: Windows reports three built-in IPv6 addresses as DNS servers. They are not used for name resolution. CERNIS shows them because Windows reports them, but does not treat them as foreign resolvers.

dnsTrust.aktionFehlerBereitsErfasst: This address is already on record.
dnsTrust.aktionFehlerUngueltig: That is not a valid IP address.

blocklist.intro: This feature checks your network's outbound contacts against publicly maintained lists and shows whether a remote endpoint is listed there as a tracker, advertising, or threat. Here you manage the list sources and set how much is shown.
blocklist.redLine: The classification comes from the named list, not from CERNIS. CERNIS only reflects it.
blocklist.ladeFehler: The lists could not be loaded. Please check that the backend is running.
blocklist.settingsFehler: The setting could not be saved.
blocklist.aktionFehler: The action could not be completed.

critical_only.label: Critical only
critical_only.hint: Shows only matches on threat lists (malware, phishing).

recommended.label: Recommended
recommended.hint: Shows threats and trackers, keeps plain advertising quiet.

all.label: Show everything
all.hint: Shows every list match, including plain advertising.

confirm.resetText: All your own lists and the entire load state will be lost; the bundled lists are recreated.

blocklist.intro: Here you maintain the lists CERNIS checks your devices' outbound contacts against – for example trackers, ads or known threats. You can switch built-in lists on and off, add or upload your own lists, and set how strictly matches are shown.
blocklist.redLine: The classification comes from the list named in each case, not from CERNIS. CERNIS only reflects it.
blocklist.ladeFehler: The lists could not be loaded.
blocklist.settingsFehler: The setting could not be saved.
blocklist.aktionFehler: The action failed. Please try again later.

critical_only.label: Critical only
critical_only.hint: Shows only matches from threat lists.

recommended.label: Recommended
recommended.hint: Shows threats as well as trackers and ads.

all.label: Show everything
all.hint: Shows all matches, including plain ads.
